data.one_liner: Widget that pretty‑prints a JSON string with customizable colors.
data.what_it_does: ColoredJson renders a JSON string as a structured, color‑coded widget. It allows developers to customize colors for keys, values, brackets, and other syntax elements.
use_when: displaying JSON data for debugging or documentation
showing API responses in a readable format
creating visual examples of JSON structures
avoid_when: handling large or streaming JSON data
performance‑critical rendering where every frame matters
weaknesses: no support for dynamic data updates
data.minimal_example:
ColoredJson(
  data: jsonEncode({
    "id": 24,
    "name": "Manthan Khandale",
    "score": 7.6,
    "hobbies": ["Music", "Filmmaking"],
    "isFlutterCool": true,
  }),
  indentLength: 5,
  keyColor: Colors.green,
  backgroundColor: Colors.black,
  boolColor: Colors.white,
  nullColor: Colors.redAccent,
  stringColor: Colors.cyan,
  curlyBracketColor: Colors.yellow,
  doubleColor: Colors.deepOrange,
  squareBracketColor: Colors.amber,
  commaColor: Colors.yellow,
  colonColor: Colors.purple,
  intColor: Colors.lime,
  textStyle: const TextStyle(fontSize: 20, letterSpacing: 2),
)
